question: An infinitely large conducting slab extends infinitely in the $x$ and $y$ directions and has thickness $2a$ along the $z$-axis, occupying $-a \le z \le +a$. It carries a steady volume current density $\vec{J}(z)=J_0\left(\frac{z}{a}\right)\hat{i}$ (current along $+x$, varying linearly with $z$). Assume the magnetic field outside the slab is zero, i.e. $\vec B=\vec 0$ for $|z|\ge a$. Determine the magnetic field $\vec{B}(z)$ at an interior point with $0<z<a$.
